title: Medicaid and CHIP coverage for pregnancy and postpartum, by state
methodology: Income limits are KFF and Georgetown CCF's 50-state survey figures as of January 2026 (KFF State Health Facts and Table 2 of the April 2026 report). They are percentages of the federal poverty level (FPL), converted to MAGI standards, and include the standard 5-percentage-point income disregard at the highest Medicaid level when the state does not cover pregnancy through CHIP. chipLimitFplPct is CHIP coverage of pregnant individuals (7 states); unbornChildLimitFplPct is CHIP's From Conception to End of Pregnancy (formerly unborn child) option (25 states); highestLimitFplPct is the highest of the three, which KFF calls the upper income limit. Postpartum status is KFF's Medicaid Postpartum Coverage Extension Tracker as of July 15, 2026. postpartumExtensionEffective is the effective date in each state's CMS approval letter (state plan amendment or section 1115 waiver), read from the documents KFF links, or the state's own announcement where noted; some states covered postpartum people for 12 months earlier with state funds or an earlier waiver (KFF). Presumptive eligibility reflects KFF/CCF's January 2025 survey (the January 2026 report does not cover it) for the Medicaid pregnancy group, updated where a state source shows a later change; it is left blank where the state did not report or we could not confirm a change. Hospitals in every state may make presumptive eligibility determinations, even in states that do not otherwise use it. Program names, agencies and application pages were checked on each state's site on 2026-10-09; Kansas, Mississippi and New Hampshire block automated checks, so their links come from the state listings on Medicaid.gov. Poverty guidelines are the 2026 HHS figures from the Federal Register. Each state's one-sentence answer is generated from these figures. Its dollar amount applies the highest income limit to the 2026 HHS guideline for a household of two (a pregnant person expecting one baby counts as two under 42 CFR 435.603), using the Alaska or Hawaii guideline where applicable. States apply their own rounding and update dates, so treat it as approximate.

povertyGuidelines2026.note: Annual income in dollars. Medicaid and CHIP limits are percentages of these figures; most programs update to new guidelines early each year.

federalFloorFplPct.text: States must cover pregnancy for individuals with income up to 138% FPL; most states (38) set the upper limit at or above 200% FPL. The median upper limit is 213% FPL (January 2026).

householdSizeRule.text: For Medicaid, a pregnant woman's family size counts her plus the number of children she is expected to deliver (42 CFR 435.603(b)).

postpartum12Month.text: Federal law requires pregnancy-related Medicaid through 60 days postpartum. The American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 gave states the option to extend it to 12 months starting April 1, 2022, and the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 made the option permanent. As of July 15, 2026, 49 states and DC have implemented 12 months (Wisconsin started July 1, 2026); Arkansas is the only state still at 60 days.

workRequirementsExemption.text: Public Law 119-21 (2025) requires states to apply Medicaid work (community engagement) requirements to expansion adults ages 19-64 starting no later than January 1, 2027 (states may start earlier; HHS may grant good-faith exemptions that end by December 31, 2028). People who are pregnant or entitled to postpartum coverage are exempt, as are parents and caretakers of a dependent child 13 or younger.

presumptiveEligibility.text: Presumptive eligibility lets qualified providers such as clinics and hospitals enroll a pregnant person in temporary Medicaid right away while the full application is processed. In January 2025, 28 states used it for pregnant people in Medicaid. Hospitals in every state may make presumptive eligibility determinations if they choose to. Alabama added it on October 1, 2025.

immigrantEligibilityChange.text: Beginning October 1, 2026, federal Medicaid and CHIP funding for non-emergency care is generally limited to U.S. citizens and nationals, lawful permanent residents, Cuban/Haitian entrants and COFA migrants. States that elected the CHIPRA 214 option may still cover lawfully residing children and pregnant women without the 5-year wait. Emergency Medicaid is not affected.

chipPostpartumRule.text: The 12-month postpartum option reaches pregnant people enrolled in CHIP's own pregnancy coverage. Coverage through CHIP's From Conception to End of Pregnancy (unborn-child) option is coverage for the baby, so the mother's postpartum coverage is limited unless the state adds it, for example through a CHIP health services initiative.

AK.summary: Alaska Medicaid (Denali KidCare) covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 230% of the federal poverty level (about $62,215 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
AK.agencyName: Alaska Department of Health, Division of Public Assistance

AL.summary: Alabama Medicaid covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 146% of the federal poverty level (about $31,594 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends. Above that, up to 317% ($68,599 for two), the ALL Babies program covers the pregnancy and about 60 days after the birth.
AL.notes: Between 146% and 317% FPL, coverage is through CHIP's From Conception to End of Pregnancy option, which covers the pregnancy (the unborn child) regardless of the parent's immigration status. Alabama started Presumptive Eligibility for Pregnancy (PEP) on October 1, 2025 (Act 2025-204), after KFF's January 2025 survey.

upperBands.postpartumText: ALL Babies, Alabama's CHIP pregnancy program run with the Department of Public Health, covers the pregnancy and the birth. Since October 1, 2024, it covers the mother through the end of the month in which the 60th day after delivery falls.
upperBands.postpartumClause: it covers the mother for only about 60 days after the birth

AR.summary: Arkansas Medicaid covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 214% of the federal poverty level (about $46,310 a year for a household of two). Its postpartum coverage ends 60 days after the pregnancy, the federal minimum.
AR.notes: Arkansas enacted presumptive eligibility for pregnant women in 2025, after KFF's January 2025 survey; we could not confirm the start date on an Arkansas DHS page. Arkansas is the only state that has not extended postpartum Medicaid to 12 months; coverage ends 60 days after pregnancy (KFF, July 2026).

AZ.agencyName: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS)

CA.summary: In California, Medi-Cal covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 213% of the federal poverty level, and the Medi-Cal Access Program (MCAP) covers it up to 322% (about $69,681 a year for a household of two). Both cover you for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
CA.agencyName: California Department of Health Care Services
CA.notes: Between 213% and 322% FPL, coverage is through CHIP's From Conception to End of Pregnancy option, which covers the pregnancy (the unborn child) regardless of the parent's immigration status. BenefitsCal is California's statewide online application for Medi-Cal and other benefits.

upperBands.postpartumText: The Medi-Cal Access Program (MCAP) covers the pregnancy above Medi-Cal's limit. Since April 1, 2022, it covers you for 12 months after the pregnancy ends, the same as Medi-Cal.

CO.summary: Health First Colorado covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 195% of the federal poverty level, and CHIP coverage (CHP+ and the unborn-child option) reaches 265% (about $57,346 a year for a household of two). Each covers you for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
CO.agencyName: Colorado Department of Health Care Policy & Financing
CO.notes: Between 260% and 265% FPL, coverage is through CHIP's From Conception to End of Pregnancy option, which covers the pregnancy (the unborn child) regardless of the parent's immigration status. Medicaid covers pregnancy up to 195% FPL and CHIP covers pregnant individuals up to 260% FPL.

upperBands.postpartumText: CHP+ covers pregnant people above Health First Colorado's limit, and since July 1, 2022 it covers you for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.

Since January 1, 2025, CHIP's From Conception to End of Pregnancy option covers pregnant people who can't get Health First Colorado or CHP+ because of immigration status, and a CHIP health services initiative covers them for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.

Florida's 12-month postpartum coverage runs through a section 1115 waiver; CMS made it effective on the effective date of Florida SB 2526 (July 1, 2022). Florida Medicaid is administered by the Agency for Health Care Administration; the Department of Children and Families (ACCESS Florida) takes applications.
FL.presumptiveEligibilityWhere: Florida's county health departments and other qualified providers can enroll you the same day through Presumptive Eligibility for Pregnant Women (PEPW), while your full Medicaid application is processed.

upperBands.postpartumText: 599 CHIP covers prenatal care and pregnancy-related services only. Cases close at the end of the birth month, or the end of the next month if the baby is born at the end of a month, so it doesn't cover the mother after birth.
upperBands.postpartumClause: it covers prenatal care only and closes at the end of the birth month

NH.summary: New Hampshire Medicaid covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 201% of the federal poverty level (about $43,496 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
NH.agencyName: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services
NH.notes: The application page blocks automated checks; the link is the state's application site as listed by the state and Medicaid.gov.

NJ.summary: In New Jersey, NJ FamilyCare covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 194% of the federal poverty level through Medicaid and up to 205% through CHIP (about $44,362 a year for a household of two). Both cover you for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
NJ.agencyName: New Jersey Department of Human Services, Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services
NJ.notes: Medicaid covers pregnancy up to 194% FPL and CHIP covers pregnant individuals up to 205% FPL. New Jersey provides 12-month postpartum coverage through a section 1115 waiver (KFF); we could not verify its effective date.

upperBands.postpartumText: NJ FamilyCare covers pregnant people above the Medicaid limit through CHIP, and its federal 1115 waiver extends that coverage to 12 months after the pregnancy ends.

NM.summary: Turquoise Care (New Mexico Medicaid) covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 255% of the federal poverty level (about $55,182 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.

NV.summary: Nevada Medicaid covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 205% of the federal poverty level (about $44,362 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
NV.notes: Nevada raised its Medicaid limit for pregnant individuals from 190% to 205% FPL, effective July 1, 2025 (CMS approval).

NY.summary: New York Medicaid covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 223% of the federal poverty level (about $48,257 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
NY.agencyName: New York State Department of Health

OH.summary: Ohio Medicaid covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 205% of the federal poverty level (about $44,362 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.

OK.summary: In Oklahoma, SoonerCare covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 210% of the federal poverty level (about $45,444 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.

OR.summary: Oregon Health Plan (OHP) covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 190% of the federal poverty level (about $41,116 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.

PA.summary: Medical Assistance (Pennsylvania Medicaid) covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 220% of the federal poverty level (about $47,608 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.

RI.summary: Rhode Island Medicaid covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 190% of the federal poverty level, and CHIP covers it up to 258% (about $55,831 a year for a household of two). Both cover you for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
RI.agencyName: Rhode Island Executive Office of Health and Human Services
RI.notes: Medicaid covers pregnancy up to 190% FPL and CHIP covers pregnant individuals up to 258% FPL.

upperBands.postpartumText: CHIP covers pregnant people above Medicaid's limit, and since October 1, 2022 it covers them for 12 months after the pregnancy ends. People covered through CHIP's unborn-child option because of immigration status get the same 12 months.

SC.summary: In South Carolina, Healthy Connections Medicaid covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 199% of the federal poverty level (about $43,064 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
SC.agencyName: South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
SC.notes: South Carolina did not report presumptive eligibility in KFF's January 2025 survey.

SD.summary: South Dakota Medicaid covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 138% of the federal poverty level (about $29,863 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
SD.agencyName: South Dakota Department of Social Services

TN.summary: In Tennessee, TennCare covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 255% of the federal poverty level (about $55,182 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.

TX.summary: Texas Medicaid for Pregnant Women covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 203% of the federal poverty level (about $43,929 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends. Between 203% and 207% ($44,795 for two), CHIP Perinatal covers the pregnancy, but the mother's coverage ends with the birth month plus two postpartum checkups.
TX.agencyName: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
TX.notes: Between 203% and 207% FPL, coverage is through CHIP's From Conception to End of Pregnancy option, which covers the pregnancy (the unborn child) regardless of the parent's immigration status.

upperBands.postpartumText: CHIP Perinatal covers the pregnancy and the birth. The mother's own coverage ends on the last day of the month the baby is born, plus two postpartum checkups within 60 days. It also covers pregnant people who can't get Medicaid because of immigration status.
upperBands.postpartumClause: the mother's coverage ends with the birth month, plus two postpartum checkups

UT.summary: Utah Medicaid covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 144% of the federal poverty level (about $31,162 a year for a household of two) and for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
UT.agencyName: Utah Department of Health and Human Services

VA.summary: Cardinal Care (Virginia Medicaid) covers pregnancy for household incomes up to 143% of the federal poverty level, and FAMIS MOMS covers it up to 205% (about $44,362 a year for a household of two). Both cover you for 12 months after the pregnancy ends; FAMIS Prenatal Coverage, for people who don't meet immigration rules, ends 60 days after the birth.
VA.agencyName: Virginia Department of Medical Assistance Services
VA.notes: Medicaid covers pregnancy up to 143% FPL and CHIP covers pregnant individuals up to 205% FPL. Virginia's 12-month postpartum coverage runs through a section 1115 waiver; the date shown is when the CMS approval took effect.

upperBands.postpartumText: FAMIS MOMS covers pregnant people above the Medicaid limit, and since July 1, 2022 it covers them for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.

immigrantCoverage.postpartumText: FAMIS Prenatal Coverage, for pregnant people who don't meet the immigration rules for Medicaid or FAMIS MOMS, covers you through 60 days after the birth.
immigrantCoverage.postpartumClause: coverage ends 60 days after the birth

WI.notes: Wisconsin began 12 months of postpartum coverage on July 1, 2026.

WV.notes: Medicaid covers pregnancy up to 185% FPL and CHIP covers pregnant individuals up to 305% FPL.

upperBands.postpartumText: WVCHIP covers pregnant people above Medicaid's limit, and since April 1, 2022 it covers them for 12 months after the pregnancy ends.
